Local PDF RAG System

A fully local question-answering pipeline over PDF books — PyMuPDF, FAISS and an Ollama model — with source citations and a retrieval evaluation.

RAGFAISSOllama

Overview

A question-answering system over PDF books that runs entirely on a local machine: no hosted LLM and no hosted vector database. Answers are generated only from retrieved passages and come with source citations.

Pipeline

flowchart TB
    A[PDF] --> B[Extraction: PyMuPDF]
    B --> C[Section-aware chunks with overlap]
    C --> D[Embeddings: all-MiniLM-L6-v2]
    D --> E[(FAISS index)]
    Q[Question] --> F[Query embedding]
    F --> E
    E --> G[Top-k chunks]
    G --> H[Ollama phi4-mini]
    H --> I[Answer with cited sources]

Design

  • Extraction and chunking: PDF text extracted with PyMuPDF, split into section-aware chunks with overlap.
  • Retrieval: embeddings from all-MiniLM-L6-v2 and exact FAISS cosine-similarity search.
  • Generation: a local Ollama model (phi4-mini) constrained to the retrieved context, with source citations.
  • Integrity checks: the index and the document store are checked for alignment, and the embedding dimension is validated, so a stale index fails loudly instead of returning wrong passages.

Evaluation

Retrieval was evaluated on a 68-question golden set.

top-k Context recall Context precision
3 0.7305 0.0445
5 0.8255 0.0427

Raising top-k from 3 to 5 increased context recall from 0.73 to 0.83. Context precision is low in absolute terms and fell slightly, so the next step is an error analysis of the failed questions before tuning chunk size or adding a reranker.

Limitations and next steps

This is a learning project, not a production service. Automated tests and CI are not in place yet. Planned: error analysis, chunk-size and reranker experiments, an API with Docker, and generation-quality evaluation.
